This is basically how it was handled last year, except they are splitting Portfolio Ops and Deal Team. Regarding Analysts - we need to provide them the bonus targets rather than Compensation just deciding. Regarding non-investment staff - again, we need to provide the targets (as we discussed earlier this week).

The biggest issue we have is how to integrate the People Systems and avoid the manual Excel–People Systems–Excel cycle we went through last year. We are working with Hannah Ferguson and People Ops on this.

VPs have to go through the final Corp-wide Charlotte review, so that is one more step for the VPs and the Investor Relations meeting outcome should be consistent with how all are rated going into the final meeting (i.e., 10/80/10, 1-100).

Jennifer

Here is our plan on Charlotte.

Analysts:

Ranked 1,2,3 by supervisors - pay determined by Me and Brandy. No meetings.

Non-investment staff but in Investor Relations:

Traditional ranking with the correct people attending the meetings. Pay grid determined by Compensation.

Associates and Senior Associates:

Ranked as per Cameron Lemmons’ percentages and then pay grid determined by Compensation.  
I would like to see 25% - 65% - 10%. Cameron disagrees. This would provide for a quick meeting rather than trying to split them into 4 groups with the top one excluding some awesome people.

Managers/Directors

Ranked from 1 to 100 in as many clusters as the groups see fit. We are going to combine managers and directors into one table. The ranking is based on this year’s performance and is directly related to pay. We will have two meetings—one for Deal Team and one for other commercial staff (Portfolio Ops/Finance/etc). We will not have a pay PRC but will take the results of the rankings and work with individual leaders after the meetings to ensure the appropriate compensation.

We will also determine promotions during this meeting using different criteria.

VPs

We will rank all our VPs from 1 to 100 with a group of selected people—some VPs and some MDs.  
This too will be directly related to pay.

Cheers as you Brits say
